title: cuda-link-timeout-breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad for an odd failure I hit on a dev box and one customer repro: long linker/dlopen stall when importing pytorch/cuda leading to test harness consuming all user memory and triggering OOM. Suspect stale stub libraries + ldconfig cache + container runtime interplay.

Symptoms observed (high level):
- Python process hangs for ~20-40s during 'import torch' inside container; while hung, CPU is low but memory steadily climbs (mmap growth) until OOM.
- nvidia-smi shows driver present, GPUs idle, no GPU memory leak.
- strace of python shows repeated open() on libcuda.so paths and long waits on futex/select around dlopen.
- dmesg occasionally shows: "NVRM: GPU at pci:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus" in a different cluster; not same machine but note.

Commands tried (copied from terminal):
- host checks:
  ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch.so | grep cuda
  # result: libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)

  ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
  # result: libcuda.so.1 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/lib/nvidia-525/libcuda.so.1

  ls -l /usr/lib/nvidia-525/libcuda.so.1
  # -> points to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/stubs/libcuda.so (STUB)  <-- suspicious

- inside container (docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint /bin/bash image:dev):
  python -c "import time; import torch; t=time.time(); torch.cuda.is_available(); print('took', time.time()-t)"
  # prints: took 32.17  (hanged then returned False)

- strace (inside container):
  strace -f -tt -o /tmp/trace python -c "import torch; torch.cuda.is_available()"
  # repeated lines: openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/stubs/libcuda.so", O_RDONLY) = 3 <0.0001>
  # then long delay: futex(0x7ffd8a..., FUTEX_WAIT_PRIVATE, ... ) = -1 EINTR <30.004>
  # dlopen attempts then EACCES/EFAULT in some cases then fallback -> CPU-only

- strace of ldd/dlopen on host: no long delays. Only inside container.

- tested with pinned driver variant in container by bind-mounting /usr/lib/nvidia-525 and setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH: 
  docker run --gpus all -v /usr/lib/nvidia-525:/host-nv -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-nv:... image:dev python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
  # returned True and instant <0.2s

Error snippets / logs captured:
- from python: RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error
- from strace: dlopen("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/stubs/libcuda.so", RTLD_NOW) = 0  # stub returns, runtime falls back
- python stack (when OOM triggers):
  MemoryError: Unable to allocate 3.5 GiB for an array with shape ...

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Stub libcuda in system path is being found inside container (packaged for compatibility), which does not provide real driver symbols. When torch chooses device, it tries to probe CUDA via dlopen and gets stub responses that cause a slow path or repeated fallbacks that leak memory in the runtime initialization code.
2) ldconfig cache inside container differs from host -> repeated searches and slow file ops cause race where process starts memory maps (maybe for pinned allocator) without successful GPU init, exhausting host RAM for large batch test harnesses.
3) nvidia-container-toolkit + runtime mounts host libcuda but permissions/selinux prevented direct open resulting in repeated retries (futex delays).
4) A race with NVML initialization: nvmlInit() times out because of driver-user mismatch and libcuda stub returns success but later fails leading to inconsistent state and high memory usage.

Quick repro plan and notes:
- Minimal reproducer created: small container that only runs python -c "import torch; torch.zeros(1024, 1024).cuda()" while monitoring memory. Repro is flaky unless stubs are mounted.
- Repro conditions that made it obvious:
  * host driver 525, container CUDA runtime 11.7 wheels (ubuntu base).
  * stale /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/stubs/libcuda.so in image created by previous apt install cuda-toolkit (left stubs).
  * starting container without --gpus or with --gpus but without mount of /usr/lib/nvidia-525 -> ended up using stubs

Mitigations tried (and which worked):
- Bind-mount host /usr/lib/nvidia-525 into container and set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-nv -> immediate success, torch.cuda.is_available() -> True, no hang, no OOM.
- Removing stub files from image (dockerfile: RUN rm -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/stubs/libcuda* ) -> also fixed.
- Upgrading nvidia-container-toolkit to latest (1.13.x) produced mixed results; mounting libs still most reliable.

Data to collect for customers/SE:
- strace around dlopen + timing (inside container)
- ldconfig -p and list of candidate libcuda paths
- full output of ldd on libtorch.so and libcudart.so in container
- `nvidia-smi -a` and driver version on host
- docker inspect, container runtime logs (/var/log/messages/journalctl -u docker or containerd)
- check for presence of stubs in image: find / -name 'libcuda*'

Next steps / TODOs: 
- Create small diagnostic script that automates checks above and prints PASS/FAIL with suggested remediation (rm stubs, bind-mount host libs). Add to runtime repo under experiments/diagnostics. (OWNER: me)
- Create a short KB for SEs describing this exact failure mode and steps to avoid when building images (tag: image-build-caveats). (OWNER: Diego)
- Add an assert in startup E2E test to detect 'stubs present inside image' and fail fast with clear message. (OWNER: Michael)
- Bisection plan if repro persists: try older driver on host (e.g., 515) vs 525; try different nvidia-container-toolkit releases.

Lessons / notes for writeup:
- This is not a classical CUDA OOM (GPU memory), it's an OOM triggered by process-level memory growth when CUDA initialization falls back incorrectly to CPU-only or does repeated file ops.
- Image hygiene matters: stubs packaged inside images are dangerous when combined with host driver mount semantics; they can cause slow or incorrect dlopen behavior.
- For customers, recommend mounting host libs or using NVIDIA container images (they handle symlinks properly).

Scratch timeline (breadcrumbs):
- 2026-02-18 09:12: start reproducer on local dev machine (driver 525)
- 2026-02-18 10:03: saw 20-30s hang + OOM in test harness; collected strace
- 2026-02-18 11:20: tried bind-mount -> immediate success
- 2026-02-19 15:45: replicated on customer staging; created patch to remove stubs from image build
- 2026-02-20 08:30: added diagnostic script to runtime experiments (WIP)

Useful one-liners for KB:
- check for stubs in image: docker run --rm image:tag sh -c "find /usr -name 'libcuda*' -print"
- print ldconfig from inside container: docker run --rm image:tag ldconfig -p | grep libcuda
- quick test whether mounting host libs fixes it: docker run --gpus all -v /usr/lib/nvidia-525:/nv /image:tag sh -c 'LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/nv python -c "import torch;print(torch.cuda.is_available())"'

Notes end.

Attachments (local): /tmp/trace (strace output), /tmp/ldconfig-before.txt, /tmp/ldconfig-after.txt

If I come back to this later: check for subtle differences in glibc versions between host and image – dlopen behavior could be influenced by symbol versioning. Also check whether container runtime is rebinding libcuda with a shim (nvidia-container-toolkit provides symlink behavior) and if that shim returns quickly but defers to slow syscall later.
